content:
Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending the deal that was set to expire in 2027. Here's what you need to know.

The renewed agreement will take effect next year

To say the relationship between Apple and Qualcomm has been rocky would be an understatement.

The two companies were once major business partners, but in 2017 they became embroiled in a massive legal battle over Qualcomm's patent licensing practices and royalty payments.

In short, Apple sued Qualcomm in U.S. federal court in early 2017, challenging its patent licensing practices and seeking approximately $1 billion in royalties that Apple claimed Qualcomm had wrongfully withheld as refunds.

This lawsuit came just three days after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) sued Qualcomm, alleging anticompetitive licensing practices. The complaint specifically referenced the deal between Qualcomm and Apple, claiming Qualcomm offered billions of dollars in conditional rebates in exchange for Apple's exclusive use of its modem chips in new iPhones and iPads.

Months later, Qualcomm countersued Apple, alleging breach of agreement and interference with its relationships with iPhone and iPad manufacturers.

The dispute was resolved in 2019 when Apple and Qualcomm agreed to withdraw all cross-litigation worldwide.

As part of the settlement, Apple made an undisclosed payment to Qualcomm, which included settling royalty disputes Apple had withheld during the litigation. The two companies also signed a six-year global patent licensing agreement and a multi-year chipset supply agreement.

That licensing agreement took effect on April 1, 2019, and included an option for Apple to extend it by two years. Apple ultimately exercised that option, extending the agreement to March 2027.

Qualcomm announced today that the two companies have renewed their agreement once again, with the new agreement set to take effect on April 1, 2027.

Qualcomm today released the following full press release:

Qualcomm Incorporated today announced it has renewed its global patent licensing agreement with Apple, with the new agreement taking effect on April 1, 2027. John Han, Senior Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL), said: "We are pleased to extend our licensing agreement with Apple."

Qualcomm has not disclosed the term of the renewed agreement, and Apple has not yet responded to the renewal.

Notably, today's announcement is separate from the much-discussed issue of Apple's use of Qualcomm modems in iPhones — Apple uses Qualcomm modems in the U.S. version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but uses its own in-house C2 modem in other regions.

Apple has not officially commented on its future modem plans, but there is widespread expectation that the company will eventually phase out Qualcomm modems entirely.
